question: Where can I get a list of wind farms in operation in Germany, with location, capacity (MW), number of turbines, operator and commissioning date?

answer.summary: The Bundesnetzagentur’s MaStR publishes onshore and offshore wind generation units, including operating status, capacity, coordinates, commissioning dates and organizational operators. It is a turbine register, not a guaranteed farm inventory: the freely entered wind-farm name is optional. Farm membership, totals and a single farm commissioning date require further verification.
main_caveats: Filter operational units; planned and retired turbines also occur. A turbine commissioning date is not necessarily the date the whole park entered service.
Wind-farm names are optional and freely chosen; aggregating them can omit turbines or combine unrelated parks.
Capacity is in kW per unit; divide by 1,000 for MW and only sum confirmed members. Operators who are natural persons and some exact coordinates are confidential.
The XML bulk download was not inspected. The extended overview has an export limit; split filters and check for missed or repeated records.
answer.confidence_reason: Field descriptions and two public unit records were inspected, but bulk extraction, farm aggregation and wider regional coverage remain unverified.

steps: Open the extended unit overview, filter wind generation units and Betriebs-Status In Betrieb, and distinguish Wind an Land from Wind auf See.
Open individual unit detail pages to verify unit identifier, status, coordinates, gross power, organizational operator and commissioning date.
The CSV overview offers filtering and export; the full public dataset is available as XML ZIP. Bulk download and aggregation have not been tested in this pass.
reading_traps: NameWindpark is optional and freely chosen, so matching names alone cannot establish a complete farm. Parey record SEE953079739183 has no park name.
Use gross kW divided by 1,000 for MW; never call one unit’s power the capacity of its entire park.
A park can comprise units commissioned on different dates; a first unit date does not establish full park commissioning.
The FAQ states 25,000 rows maximum for the extended overview and 5,000 for the current overview.
Exact locations of units at or below 30 kW and natural-person information are withheld.

steps: Open the feature-list URL; the returned HTML lists a total and individual records with status, dates and coordinates.
Inspect planstd and retain am Netz for grid-connected units; distinguish genehmigt and beantragt.
The view paginates. A request with f=html&limit=10&offset=40 returned page 5. Assess UTM reference system and field definitions before reuse.
For Hessen, read anlagen.csv as CSV with quoted multiline fields; select anlagenstatus = in Betrieb, and examine name_windpark and unit identifiers.
The first two Offheim records both state 0.6 MW and share a park name: together they sum to 1.2 MW, but no complete park membership has been established.
Anlagen CSV uses EPSG:25832 UTM coordinates; join permit tables by id_wea only as documented in the README.
reading_traps: The displayed count includes all stages, not only operating turbines.
windpark is a yes/no flag, not a park identifier; the examples do not establish full park membership.
Records in the web tool can be cached snapshots. Unit of nennleist and current service currency require further verification.
Hessen inbetrieb_altanlanz means commissioning OR notice of an existing installation, not always a verified commissioning date.
CSV contains quoted embedded newlines, so physical line counts are not record counts.
Hessen and MaStR differ in reporting parties and may disagree because of timing or entry differences.
